text:
mari-plat: Proposal: convert billing_metrics.route_id from text to bigint using a tenant-scoped migration. We discovered route_id_text is always a numeric fingerprint for ~98% of rows. Moving to bigint will cut GROUP BY latency significantly.

sophia: Love the perf win. Concern: wide table + retention means backfill IO could be huge. Need clear compatibility/rollback plan.

anil: Plan idea: add route_id_int bigint NULL, add migration_status enum (pending|in_progress|done), dual-write at ingest behind a feature flag. Reads use an adapter that prefers route_id_int when non-null.

mari-plat: Exactly. Steps I suggest: 1) add columns (no index) 2) enable dual-write in canary ingest pool 3) run tenant-by-tenant backfill with rate limits and mark migration_status per-tenant 4) switch console and batch jobs to prefer int for canary tenants 5) after 30d stable, create CONCURRENT index on route_id_int and drop text.

gabe: Table size numbers?

mari-plat: ~1.2B rows across all tenants (6mo retention). Peak daily insert ~6M rows. Backfill worst-case is ~1B rows but we'll only backfill active tenants first.

jess: Strongly prefer tenant-windowing for backfill. Don't do a single global UPDATE. We should also maintain a small migration control table: tenant_id, status, last_processed_ts, error_count.

anil: For indexes: avoid creating a global index during dual-write. Create per-tenant partial index or wait until backfill marks tenant done, then create CONCURRENT index scoped via WHERE tenant_id = X? PostgreSQL doesn't support per-tenant indexes, but partial index with tenant predicate for big tenants is doable.

sophia: Console impact: dashboards and saved queries must be tolerant. UI should show "legacy id" badge when route_id_int is null. We should expose a feature flag to flip prefer_route_id_int for tenants.

gabe: Billing batch jobs must be synchronized to use the same read adapter or results will diverge. I'll update the nightly pipeline to read via the adapter layer.

jess: Add telemetry: backfill_rows_processed, backfill_error_rate, fallback_reads_pct, avg_query_ms_by_column. Create dashboards before starting.

sre-oncall: Runbook needs rollback steps: 1) disable dual-write, 2) point reads to route_id_text, 3) stop backfill jobs. Schedule schema add during low traffic window (Fri 02:00 UTC).

mari-plat: Drafted example backfill SQL (run in small batches with sleep):

UPDATE billing_metrics
SET route_id_int = CASE WHEN route_id_text ~ '^[0-9]+$' THEN route_id_text::bigint ELSE NULL END,
    migration_status = 'in_progress'
WHERE tenant_id = :TENANT
  AND route_id_int IS NULL
LIMIT 100000;

mari-plat: We will run a loop that records rows_updated and last_processed_id in migration control table. Unparsable route_id_text values get logged and aggregated into a mapping table for manual review.

anil: Consider copy-to-new-table for very large tenants: create new_billing_metrics with desired schema, populate in parallel with concurrency, then swap with minimal downtime. pg_repack style or logical copy might help avoid bloating primary table. Tradeoffs: complexity and extra storage.

sophia: We need to update docs: console API changelog, observability docs, and runbook. Also add a subtle UI note: "If you see 'legacy id' badges contact support".

gabe: Exports: nightly S3 dumps currently denormalize route fields. Export pipeline must adopt the read adapter to include route_id_int values post-migration. I'll own export changes.

jess: QA plan: provision two canary tenants that mimic heavy billing patterns. Run the full path: ingest -> backfill -> batch billing -> console dashboards, compare aggregates. Tolerances: counts must match within 0.01% after adapter switch.

sre-oncall: Alerting: create an alert if fallback_reads_pct > 1% for a cohort after migration, or if backfill error_rate > 0.5%. Also watch DB IO: avg_write_latency and checkpoint storms.

anil: Indexing plan after stable: for tenants marked done, create index CONCURRENTLY on route_id_int (WITH (fillfactor=80)). Then drop old index on route_id_text and finally drop column route_id_text after a 90d safety window.

mari-plat: I'll open PRs: schema migration SQL, ingest dual-write feature flag, read-adapter change, backfill orchestration job + migration control table, dashboards, and runbook.

sophia: I'll own console read-adapter PRs and UI changes.

anil: I'll build the orchestrator for tenant cohorts and the per-tenant partial index plan.

gabe: I'll update billing jobs and export pipeline to read from adapter.

jess: I'll create canary tenants and run QA scripts.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: billing-ingest-v3 -> canary-pool-3 at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z :white_check_mark: 

mari-plat: Timeline: start schema addition 2026-03-23 02:00 UTC, enable dual-write on canary pool same day, begin backfill cohorts next day. Cohort ramp over 14 days. Full index/drop after 60 days stable.

sophia: Don't forget to update ACLs and KMS annotations if any exported snapshots include route ids.

mari-plat: Good catch. Gabe will verify export encryption and metadata.

jess: Final note: keep migration_status visible in the admin console so support can see tenant progress.

mari-plat: Thanks all — I'll post the runbook PR and a checklist. We'll reconvene after first canary run. :rocket:
